subject: Orionix inference discovery — recap, SLOs & proposed topology
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Byrne <alex@orionix.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Nov 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Orionix inference discovery — recap, SLOs & proposed topology

Hi Alex — thanks again for the time this morning. Below is a brief recap of what we heard, the risks/opportunities, and a lightweight proposal for next steps so we can get your infra and SRE teams aligned before the technical deep-dive.

High-level pain points (from our call)
- Customer-facing chat API must hit p95 <= 150ms for short prompts (system + user ~<256 tokens).
- Steady-state traffic ~400 qps; heavy spikes up to 1,200 qps during batch events (10–20 minutes).
- Cost is a major constraint for the product team — need predictable unit economics and ability to throttle cost during non-peak windows.
- Data residency & encryption: keys managed in customer KMS; audit logs required for certain endpoints.

Goals you stated
- Baseline throughput with <200ms median and p95 <= 150ms for 95% of traffic classes.
- Graceful degradation: when capacity constrained, fall back to a smaller model with no hard failures.
- Ability to run a canary rollout for model updates and a fast rollback path.

Redwood recommended topology (initial proposal)
1) Dedicated latency pool for production-critical traffic (pin to high-priority GPUs) — supports the 150ms p95 goal for short prompts.
2) Burst/spot pool for handling 1,200 qps spikes; automatic routing policy to overflow to less-expensive model variants.
3) KV/prefix cache in front of the runtime for repeated context to reduce token generation and cost (~30–40% token savings for typical flows).
4) Quantized model variant (int8 or q4) for the burst path to control cost while maintaining acceptable quality.
5) Canary rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic quality checks against your prompt set.

Immediate asks / next steps
- Can you share a week of anonymized traffic (sampled requests + size distribution) and a couple of representative payloads (up to 1k tokens)? This helps us size batching and memory/KV cache.
- Align a technical deep-dive with your infra/SRE (we suggested Dec 2) — Karthik will lead the runtime topology conversation.
- I attached a draft mutual action plan for timelines and owners (mutual_action_plan_draft.xlsx).

If anything above is off, call it out and I will update. Otherwise I’ll queue a calendar invite for Dec 2 at 10:00 PT with a short agenda: traffic shape, SLOs, KMS/encryption, canary plan, and procurement checklist.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Naomi — really helpful summary, thanks. Two quick corrections and a couple of asks from our side.

Correction on SLOs:
- Our product SLA target for API responses is p95 <= 120ms for conversational/short-turn flows (we were conservative on the call; 150ms is the long-term business ceiling but the product team wants tighter).

Traffic clarifying detail:
- Steady-state is ~400 qps as you noted, but spikes to 1,200 qps are often very short (3–8 minutes) and driven by scheduled batches. We care most about minimizing failed requests during spikes rather than keeping all p95 targets perfect.

Procurement / compliance asks:
- Can you send a high-level SOC 2 summary and your standard procurement contract? Procurement prefers a doc we can kick off in parallel with the POC.

We’ll share an anonymized sampling of traffic and two example payloads by EOD today. Please include an estimate ballpark for monthly cost at the steady-state and for a typical spike (assume 1,200 qps for 10 minutes).

Thanks — looking forward to the Dec 2 deep-dive.
Alex Byrne
Head of Platform, Orionix Labs

Alex / Naomi — quick technical notes ahead of the Dec 2 call so your infra team has something concrete to react to. I’ll expand on these during the deep-dive.

Sizing & topology proposal (technical)
- Dedicated pool: target steady 400–500 qps with p95 <= 120ms for short prompts. Rough starting point: 4x A100/80GB-equivalent instances (model-dependent) with persistent model residency (no cold loads).
- Burst pool: autoscaled instances tied to a lower-cost instance type with quantized model (int8/q4). Overflow routing should prefer the quantized variant with a graceful signaling header so clients can detect quality-switch.
- Batching & latency: set continuous batching window to 8–12ms with max batch size tuned by observed tokens per request; prefix/KV cache should aim to keep the 95th-percentile context hits in memory — we’ll need sample payloads to size this.
- KV cache sizing: initial estimate 30–40GB depending on your session/turn retention; we’ll confirm once we see the sample traffic.

Quality & rollout
- Canary plan: 5% (smoke), automated prompt-set evals and latency checks for 24h -> 25% -> 100% if no regressions.
- Fallbacks: route to smaller full-precision model for very latency-sensitive calls (if quantized variant has quality issues).

Security/operations asks
- Confirm whether keys are in your KMS (yes/no) and whether you require HSM-level attestations.
- Do you need request-level audit logs retained for >1 year? That changes storage cost/retention plan.

Deliverables before Dec 2 call
1) Orionix to share: 1 week sampled traffic + two representative requests (anonymized).
2) Redwood to produce: rough cost estimate for steady-state and for a 10-minute 1,200 qps spike (ballpark), and a deployment topology diagram for review.

Happy to sync on any of the above prior to the deep-dive.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
